title: Per-tenant reserved throttle smoothing and amnesty logging
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Introduce a per-tenant smoothing layer on top of the existing dedicated pool rate limiter to reduce false SLA credit churn and enable short 'amnesty' windows for brief spikes caused by garbage events (e.g., warmup storms, single-batch spikes). This ticket implements the accounting and logging surface required for transparent, auditable retroactive adjustments without changing the visible committed throughput contract for customers.
background: Problem: Brief, high-frequency micro-bursts often trigger burst accounting events that create noisy SLA credits and customer support touchpoints. Current system immediately debits burst buckets, which leads to frequent small retroactive credits and difficult reconciliation for customers.
Goal: Smooth transient burst accounting while retaining precise, auditable ledgers so customers and finance can reproduce every adjustment.
Design constraints: must preserve exact per-request attribution (tenant, reservation_id, pool_id), be O(1) on the hot path, and support retroactive reconciliation for up to 72 hours of lookback.
proposal_summary: Add a lightweight moving-average smoothing layer on burst counters. Each tenant maintains a smoothed_throughput value computed with exponential decay (alpha configurable per org). Short spikes are absorbed into smoothing and do not immediately reduce available burst tokens until smoothing exceeds configured thresholds.

Introduce 'amnesty tokens' that temporarily allow transient overage without immediate billing debit. Amnesty tokens are minted from a per-reservation micro-escrow funded by historical underuse (if enabled) or as a time-limited grace budget for new tenants. Amnesty usage is logged and available for reconciliation.

Persist every amortized adjustment into the event-sourced ledger (billing_events_v2) with the following tags: original_request_id, request_ts, reservation_id, pre_smooth_value, post_smooth_value, amnesty_consumed, raw_token_delta. This keeps the hot path constant-time while enabling full forensic replay offline.
Expose new console metrics and billing export fields: smoothed_rate, smoothing_alpha, amnesty_balance, smoothing_trigger_count, retro_adjustment_flag.
technical_notes: Smoothing algorithm: smoothed_t(t) = alpha * observed_t + (1 - alpha) * smoothed_t(prev). Default alpha = 0.15 (~half-life ~4.2 min) configurable per-reservation via the Dedicated API.

Amnesty policy: allow up to 'A' tokens in a rolling window of 'W' seconds. For customers with historical underutilization, convert a fraction of past unused reserved throughput into amnesty_balance at month boundary (configurable factor f). Amnesty expiry is set to 72h by default.

Hot path changes: rate limiter will consult (smoothed_throughput, amnesty_balance) instead of raw burst counter. On accept, emit a lightweight log record to an append-only buffer for batching into billing_events_v2. No synchronous DB writes on accept to preserve p99 latency.

Reconciliation: offline job will consume batched events and compute final debits/credits. Any amnesty-used entries produce an audit transaction and (if configured) a customer-visible memo on the invoice. Retroactive credits are batched hourly with a visible 'amnesty-adjustment' line item.

Performance: additional CPU per request is a single multiply/add for smoothing + a branch. Memory: maintain one float and one small int per active tenant in the in-memory limiter table. Back-of-envelope: <2% p50 CPU overhead in 95th-percentile traffic shapes measured on local perf harness.

Failure modes: if event-batch job fails, we keep a conservative escrow to avoid over-crediting; the ledger writer will retry with exponential backoff and tombstone bad events after operator review. We will surface a dedicated alert channel for reconciliation backlog > 30 minutes.

Security/Compliance: billing_events_v2 contains per-request metadata and must be encrypted at rest and access-controlled. Flagging 'security_review_required': true for the central ledger storage changes (see 'security_review_required' field).

Backward compatibility: customers who have explicitly opted out of smoothing/amnesty via their reservation metadata will continue to be billed under legacy behavior. The Dedicated API will accept 'billing_behavior: legacy|smoothed' during reservation update.
acceptance_criteria: Unit + integration tests for smoothing math with deterministic seed and boundary cases (alpha=0, alpha=1, high-frequency spikes).
End-to-end canary against a single low-risk tenant: observe no increase in customer-visible SLA credit noise for 7 days under synthetic spike load.
Billing export includes new columns and matches retroactive audit run for 72h of historical events (replay produces identical invoice lines).
Dashboard panels added: smoothed_rate over time, amnesty_balance per reservation, reconciliation backlog metric. Alerts fire if reconciliation job lag > 30m.
PRD reviewer sign-off from Finance and Customer Support with explicit example walkthroughs for customer inquiries.
Security review completed for ledger changes and encryption knobs documented in the change request.
tasks: Design: finalize alpha defaults and amnesty sizing knobs (owner: Alex Chen).
Runtime: implement smoothed counters and amnesty fast-path in rate-limiter (owner: S. Nunez).
Ledger: add billing_events_v2 schema and batch writer with idempotency keys (owner: Miguel Rivera).
Console: add metric panels and billing CSV column mapping (owner: Jordan Lee).
Reconciler job: implement replay and retro-credit batching with audit exports (owner: Priya Kapoor).
Canary rollout: prepare tenant onboarding flow and migration scripts (owner: Solutions Eng).
Documentation: update Dedicated API docs and billing FAQ (owner: DevRel).
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable for 1-3 low-risk tenants via reservation flag for 7 days. Monitor reconciliation metrics and support tickets.
Phase 2 (opt-in): allow customers to opt-in via Console and Dedicated API for next 2 weeks after canary success.
Phase 3 (default opt-out): enable platform-wide smoothing for new reservations. Existing reservations default to legacy unless customer flips flag.
Data migration: nightly job to seed initial smoothed_t values from last 30m of raw throughput. Amnesty balances seeded from last-month underutilization with factor f=0.25 by default.
Rollback: use reservation flag to instantly revert to legacy behavior. Retro credits from canary run are idempotent and reversible by ledger adjustments if necessary.
observability: Metrics to add: dedicated.reservation.smoothed_rate, dedicated.reservation.raw_rate, dedicated.reservation.amnesty_balance, billing.reconciler.lag_seconds
Traces: include smoothing decision span in the request trace when smoothing prevents a debit action (tag: smoothing.v=alpha),
Logs: structured append-only logs for every amortized event with idempotency key and tenant tags. Persist to S3 partitioned by date for >1 year retention for audit.
notes: Stakeholders: Finance (billing accuracy), Customer Support (investigate fewer noisy credits), Platform Reliability (no p99 regression).
Open questions: optimal default alpha across diverse workloads; whether amnesty should be bill-visible or only a reconciliation-only mechanism. Action: A/B test with opt-in cohort.
Related doc: design sketch in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DED/Smoothed+Burst+Accounting
